title: Treacle Tart
subtitle: Golden syrup tart with a lemon and breadcrumb filling
excerpt: A buttery shortcrust case filled with golden syrup, fresh breadcrumbs, lemon zest, and cream, baked until set and sticky. The most quintessentially British dessert there is.

recipe.sourceNotes: Treacle tart was first recorded in British recipe books in the 1880s, shortly after Lyle's Golden Syrup was first produced in 1885 and quickly became a household staple. The name is slightly misleading: the tart uses golden syrup (light treacle), not the darker black treacle. The filling is simply golden syrup extended with fresh breadcrumbs, which absorb the syrup and give it body, and sharpened with lemon juice to cut the sweetness. It was famously cited by Harry Potter as his favourite pudding.

content.text: Blind bake the pastry case before adding the filling or the base will be soggy. Warm the golden syrup before mixing: cold syrup is too thick to incorporate evenly. The tart is done when the filling is just set around the edges and no longer wobbles in the middle when the tin is shaken. It will firm up further as it cools.

Heat the oven to 200 C / fan 180 C / gas 6. Roll the pastry to line a 23 cm tart tin. Chill for 20 minutes. Blind bake with baking paper and weights for 15 minutes. Remove the paper and weights and bake for a further 5 minutes until pale gold.
Reduce the oven to 170 C / fan 150 C / gas 3. Warm the golden syrup in a saucepan until runny. Remove from heat. Stir in the breadcrumbs, lemon zest, and lemon juice. Beat in the cream and egg.

Pour the filling into the pastry case. Bake for 25 to 30 minutes until the filling is set and just golden. Cool for at least 20 minutes before slicing. Serve warm or at room temperature with clotted cream or ice cream.
